reviews.t: Recommended by a speech-language pathologist to help feeding skills
reviews.x: I don't know about this product being a "toy", but it was recommended by a speech-language pathologist (SLP) to help with some mechanical feeding problems. Our little one has had a hard time with textures in food, among other things.  It's a great teether, and has actually helped with feeding, too. I use one of those sippy-cup straps to attach it to the high chair, and he'll chew on it between bites. I could see using it as a toothbrush, which is probably its intended purpose, but for now, it's

reviews.t: It only took a few times and he was good to go
reviews.x: I have no idea why this works but my little one was having trouble figuring out how to chew and swallow his solid food.  My pediatrician told me about this and said you just rub it on the inside of their cheeks a couple times a day.  It only took a few times and he was good to go. So weird but glad it worked!

reviews.t: Waste of money for older kids with ASD
reviews.x: My son bit the rubber top off with in the first fifteen minutes. Waste of money for older kids with ASD.

reviews.t: Using for Speech Therapy -- Great idea
reviews.x: We ordered this because of the recommendation from our 2.5 year old's speech therapist.  Apparently it's good to show them how to move their tongue and where to place it when saying certain words or sounds (like EEEEEE or D and T).  Works great for this purpose.

reviews.t: Good tool for food training for our baby
reviews.x: No complaints about this Nuk Brush.  Our baby has food sensitivity for which she is seeing a speech pathologist.  She recommended that baby always has something to keep her busy in the high chair to prevent her from getting bored and playing with the food that she's supposed to eat and not play with.  She gave us something similar to this and our baby really took to it and chewed on it, which also helps stimulate her mouth to help her reduce her sensitivity.  The dogs got to the one the speech p

reviews.t: My son has oral sensory issues and a massaging toothbrush was recommended. This item would have been fine other than ...
reviews.x: I guess it's my fault for seeing "massaging" and thinking that meant vibrating.  I'm not sure what makes this worth $11 then.  My son has oral sensory issues and a massaging toothbrush was recommended.  This item would have been fine other than the fact that it is dirty.  No refunds so I'm stuck with a gross brush that we won't use.  Not happy.

reviews.t: Nuk brush great for SPD chewing needs
reviews.x: Our two-year-old has sensory processing issues and needs to have safe "chewies."  The nuk brush is one of his favorites.  We also feel that it has helped to get him more used to tooth brushing.

Our speech pathologist suggested we get the Nuk for our daughter to help stimulate her tongue and gums, to encourage her to eat and to teach her how to use her tongue.  It's worked OK for us, but for what it is, it's expensive.  Additionally, I would love to see this version come with the round "stopper" the toothbrush comes with, to help prevent her from sticking the Nuk too far into her mouth.

My son has oral sensitivity. This brush is a great product. We have been told that it helps in reducing texture issues and it seem to be helping. Great product! I wish they have more options like these for the kids to over come oral aversion!
I thought this had vibration. Very misleading and waste of money. Trashed it!

I liked this product. The first time my daughter has it she loved it. but that lasted a day. She just gets over things quickly. My daughter is 2 1/2 and she likes to put things in her mouth since she has sensory issues. I was very excited about this and was recommended by her ABA Therapist but it didnt keep her interest long.

As a mum of autistic toldder ( 2 years old) is so hard anything I try! Him had sensory disorder, part of therapy is massage his gums, but really this product is not for kiddos with this issue. At the first time of used my son bit it so hard. I was so lucky to take off his mouth completed. That maybe woks but for autistic kids NO! I was want send it back but I must take time for drop in a locker or pay 💰! Again for this .
I am sure this is great for a teething baby. If you are thinking about buying for an ASD child, do not bother. My 4 year old ASD son had the tip chewed off in less than an hour.

I got this hoping it would be a good alternative to the Z-Vibe tool with a similar design. It didn't work well for use as a Vagus Nerve stimulation device unfortunately. It's a bit uncomfortable to use on the ear as the tip isn't as soft as I thought it would be.  It would, however, be great for teething purposes so it does what it says it does.

reviews.t: I have a child with autism who loves these Nuk brushes to satisfy the need for some sensory input in his mouth
reviews.x: I'll start by saying that I bought this product for a use that it's not intended for. I have a child with autism who loves these Nuk brushes to satisfy the need for some sensory input in his mouth. These brushes are just not built to be chewed on constantly and if that's what you need you should check out the items sold by Ark.  That said, my son loves these to chew on, they just don't last long enough for that purpose. I know they are not meant to be chewed on, but I  would love if they made a

This product is great for kiddos who need help developing their senses in their mouth.  My boy has oral motor (tongue) issues and may not be able to feel things inside his mouth like the typical 3 year old.  I use it after brushing every night to help improve his oral motor and sense.  My kid has no problem brushing, so it's easy to use this Nuk brush with him.

reviews.t: Helps Desensitize Baby To Solid Food and Texture
reviews.x: We're currently using this to desensitize my son to food textures and solid foods after his (fully repaired) cleft palate surgery left him with oral aversion. So far, we're seeing progress. I'm hoping he will get on to eating a full array of food soon.
Disgusting!  Came damaged and bent with chew marks!!!!!  Don’t buy!!!!
the best thing for my three year old thank you thank you
Great sensory tool even if not using for teething

reviews.t: Purchase the brush because my daughter's OT recommended it for her for her sensory needs
reviews.x: Purchase the brush because my daughter's OT recommended it for her for her sensory needs. I got two and realize it was a waste of time. She chewed up these brushes in under a week. Yes I only gave it to her when she asked for it, but it was nothing but a nub in 5 days. Wish I would have found something else to use instead of this for her mouth sensory needs.

reviews.t: This was recommended for us through our son's OT
reviews.x: This was recommended for us through our son's OT.  Our son has learned the motions of spoon feeding well through this item, to the point where now he just needs to learn how to position a real spoon sideways instead of vertically in his mouth.  This is nothing special, but still a quality product that serves its purpose for a good price.

WARNING, this does not vibrate at all. So, it is NOT like the Z-Vibe oral motor tool.  Maybe, just maybe, this is good for an adult to use for therapeutic oral motor stimulation. It is so hard on the gums that a child, or anyone with sensitive gums will be in pain biting down on this.

reviews.t: My occupational therapist recommended this as a tool to help desensitize my daughter ...
reviews.x: My occupational therapist recommended this as a tool to help desensitize my daughter and help her chew with her back teeth. (We are in feeding therapy for low tone). It seems to be working, and she definitely doesn't mind it going into her mouth. She will pick it up and chew on it.

So far my kid loves chewing on this. Didn’t even have to ask him to he just picked it up and started knawing on it. Those molars have been awful and this has helped. Also needed him to use his tongue muscles more to improve his speech so we’re hoping this helps as well.

claims.text: Many reviewers say it was recommended by a speech-language pathologist or therapist and helped with feeding, chewing, or tongue skills.
Several parents of children with sensory issues report it works well as a safe chewy or for oral sensitivity.
Some reviewers complain it is expensive or not worth the price for what it is.
Multiple reviewers report the rubber tip was chewed off quickly, especially by older children with ASD, making it unsuitable for them.
A few reviewers were misled into thinking it vibrates or is electric.
